name: Jellyfish
description: 600 million years of evolution without brain, heart, or blood. Distributed nerve net coordinates bell contractions for jet propulsion. Turritopsis dohrnii achieves biological immortality through transdifferentiation. Bioluminescent pulse signaling in deep ocean.

core_attributes.neurology: diffuse nerve net, no central brain, rhopalia sensory clusters
core_attributes.pattern: bioluminescent pulse signaling, biological immortality, jet propulsion rhythm

scope.definition: Proportion of bioluminescent jellyfish light pulses that elicit a measurable response (avoidance or attraction) in co-occurring organisms, measured in mesocosm behavioral assays.

evidence.source: Haddock et al. (2010) 'Bioluminescence in the Sea', Annual Review of Marine Science 2:443-493; Widder (2010) 'Bioluminescence in the ocean: origins of biological, chemical, and ecological diversity', Science 328:704-708.
cross_domain_examples: Aequorea victoria GFP-based bioluminescence: counter-predator startle response in >80% of predator trials
deep-sea Vampyroteuthis bioluminescence: prey attraction and predator deterrence in low-light zone
dinoflagellate bioluminescent waves: wave-triggered flashes warn predators of fish school presence

scope.falsifiability: If bioluminescent pulses in controlled mesocosms produce no differential behavioral response in co-occurring organisms compared to dark controls, signaling function is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Signaling function is highly context-dependent — the same flash can attract prey or deter predators depending on species and depth. Deep-sea measurement requires ROV observation with minimal light contamination.

scope.definition: Proportion of somatic cell types in Turritopsis dohrnii that successfully transdifferentiate into totipotent cyst cells during reverse-development, enabling biological rejuvenation.

evidence.source: Piraino et al. (1996) 'Reversing the life cycle', Biological Bulletin 190:302-312; De Rosa et al. (2019) transdifferentiation mechanism in Turritopsis.
cross_domain_examples: T. dohrnii completes medusa→polyp reversal under stress, expressing Oct4/Sox2 pluripotency markers
salamander limb regeneration: dedifferentiation to progenitor state before redifferentiation — partial analogue
iPSC reprogramming (Yamanaka 2006): artificial transdifferentiation using same pluripotency factor logic

scope.falsifiability: If T. dohrnii cysts formed during reverse-development cannot produce full medusa in controlled culture, the biological immortality claim (indefinite rejuvenation) fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Reverse development has been induced in lab but frequency in wild is unknown. Lab reverse-development rate ~0.65-0.80 under stress conditions. Aging may still occur at molecular level despite cellular rejuvenation.

scope.definition: Froude propulsion efficiency of jellyfish bell-pulsing locomotion — ratio of useful thrust to total hydrodynamic power input — measured via PIV (particle image velocimetry) wake analysis.

evidence.source: Dabiri et al. (2005) 'Flow patterns generated by oblate medusan jellyfish', Journal of Experimental Biology 208:1257-1265; Colin & Costello (2002) hydrodynamic analysis.
cross_domain_examples: oblate jellyfish (Aurelia): Froude efficiency 0.82-0.90 — higher than prolate (0.55-0.70)
jellyfish leading-edge vortex ring entrains ambient fluid, reducing power cost by 30% vs solid body
scallop clap-and-fling swimming: analogous vortex-ring propulsion at low Reynolds number
human-designed underwater ROV: 0.65-0.75 Froude efficiency — jellyfish beats most engineered alternatives

scope.falsifiability: If PIV wake analysis shows jellyfish propulsive efficiency below 0.70, the vortex-ring momentum transfer model is incorrect.
scope.measurement_limits: Efficiency is bell-shape dependent — oblate (moon jellyfish) outperforms prolate (lion's mane) by 25%. Cold water increases viscosity and reduces efficiency. Measurement requires controlled flow tank without walls.
